title: Career Roadmap · Security Operations Technician
summary: A Security Operations Technician helps monitor security alerts, investigate suspicious activity, review logs, support incident response and protect an organization’s computers, networks and cloud systems.

facts.Course: Diploma - Cyber Security / AI / Data Analytics / Cloud

about.label: Common pathway
about.text: Class 10/12 → IT / Networking diploma or related degree → cybersecurity labs + practical training → SOC / Security Operations Technician → Security Analyst.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Science with Mathematics is useful; eligibility for IT diplomas and degrees varies.

blocks.label: Useful subjects
blocks.text: Computer Science, Mathematics, English and basic electronics.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Networking, operating systems, cybersecurity fundamentals and ethical computing.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Logical reasoning, careful documentation, troubleshooting and attention to detail.

blocks.label: Entrance
blocks.text: Polytechnic and degree admission routes depend on the state and institution. Verify current official notifications.

items.text: Diploma in Computer Engineering / IT → Hardware, operating systems and networking foundations.
Diploma in Cybersecurity / Networking → Security monitoring and incident-response foundations; verify course recognition.
BCA / B.Sc. Computer Science or IT → Systems, networking and security operations.
B.Tech. Computer Science / IT → Broader cybersecurity engineering pathways.
B.Sc. Cybersecurity, where offered → Dedicated security studies and practical labs.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: Requirements vary by institution. A diploma may help with entry-level technical roles; some employers prefer a degree for security analyst positions.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Networking, Windows/Linux basics, cybersecurity principles and system logs.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Security monitoring, alert triage, endpoint protection and incident documentation.

blocks.label: Year 3
blocks.text: SIEM tools, threat investigation, log analysis and practical labs.

blocks.label: Year 4, if applicable
blocks.text: Advanced incident-response project, internship and job preparation.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Analyze sample security logs; build a basic SIEM lab; investigate simulated phishing alerts; write an incident-response report.

blocks.label: Government / research
blocks.text: CERT-In resources and advisories, academic cybersecurity labs and eligible public-sector IT security teams.

blocks.label: Private sector
blocks.text: Security Operations Centres (SOCs), managed security service providers, IT consulting firms and enterprise security teams.

blocks.label: Potential employers
blocks.text: Cybersecurity service providers, banks, telecom companies and large IT firms; check official career portals.

blocks.label: Ideal areas
blocks.text: Alert triage, log analysis, vulnerability tracking and incident documentation.
Internships and vacancies are not guaranteed. Practice only in authorized labs or systems.

blocks.label: Alternative
blocks.text: Diploma → BCA / B.Sc. IT / B.Tech. → cybersecurity specialization.

blocks.text: Useful certifications

items.text: CompTIA Security+ — broad cybersecurity foundations.
Cisco CCST Cybersecurity — entry-level security concepts.

Microsoft Security Operations Analyst Associate (SC-200) — intermediate certification covering security monitoring, threat investigation and response using Microsoft security tools.
Microsoft Learn
